frameData.name: Lancaster
frameData.description:
The IPS-N Lancaster is a mil-spec variant of an older IPS-N civilian terrestrial, inter/outer-hull transport and maintenance chassis, streamlined for use in any theater. The Lancaster features multiple redundant systems and sophisticated interaction projectors to ensure pinpoint accuracy when engaging with delicate systems, whether damaged or intact.
Lancaster pilots often adopt roles as sappers and engineers in frontline support. Sometimes ridiculed for piloting the old-fashioned frame by newer, untested pilots, veteran Lancaster jockeys know the truth: the Lancaster is one of the most reliable and well-made mechs out there, indispensable on any serious long-range mission. Not every mission is won with bullets, lasers, and bombs: without the engineers and their Lannies, few of those hotshots would come home alive.

traits.name: Insulated
traits.description: The Lancaster has Immunity to burn.

traits.name: Combat Repair
traits.description: In combat, the Lancaster can use 4 Repairs to repair a destroyed mech as a full action, returning it to 1 Structure, 1 Stress, and 1 HP.

actions.name: Combat Repair
actions.detail: Use 4 Repairs to repair a destroyed mech as a full action, returning it to 1 Structure, 1 Stress, and 1 HP.

traits.name: Redundant Systems
traits.description: At your discretion, other characters adjacent to the Lancaster can spend its Repairs as their own.

active_effects.name: Redundant Systems
active_effects.detail: Other characters adjacent to your Lancaster can spend its Repairs as their own.

core_system.name: Latch Drone
core_system.description: Known colloquially as a “Wingman”, latch drones are companion drones carried by and deployed from a chassis. Pilots are recommended not to develop emotional attachments to these drones due to their high casualty rate.
core_system.active_effect:
Your Latch Drone clamps onto an allied mech within its Range. For the rest of the scene you take 1 heat at the start of each of your turns, but your target gains +1 accuracy on all attacks, checks, and saves, and Immunity to the Impaired, Jammed, Slowed, Shredded, and Immobilized conditions from characters other than itself. This effect ends if either character becomes Stunned.
While this system is active, you cannot use the Latch Drone for any other purpose.

active_effects.name: Supercharger
active_effects.detail: Your target gains +1 accuracy on all attacks, checks, and saves, and Immunity to the Impaired, Jammed, Slowed, Shredded, and Immobilized conditions from characters other than itself. This effect ends if either character becomes Stunned.

data.name: Cable Winch System

actions.detail:
These cables can be attached to an adjacent character. If the target is Stunned or willing, you automatically succeed; otherwise, they can resist with a successful Hull save. Once attached, you and the target may not move more than 5 spaces away from each other. Either character can tow the other, obeying the normal rules for lifting and dragging, and becoming Slowed while doing so.
Any character can remove the cables on a hit with a melee attack or Improvised Attack against Evasion 10.
These cables can also be used to drag, pull, or otherwise interact with objects and the environment. They are 5 spaces long and can support a combined Size 6 before they break. Characters can use them to climb surfaces, allowing them to climb without a Speed penalty.

data.description: A winch system consists of an externally mounted spool of nanocarbon-weave cable and a recovery subroutine installed on the mech.

data.name: Restock Drone
data.effect: Expend a charge to deploy a restock drone to any free, adjacent space, where it primes at the end of your turn.

deployables.name: Restock Drone
deployables.detail: While adjacent to this drone, allied characters can activate it as a quick action, clearing 1d6 heat and one condition, and reloading one Loading weapon. After being activated, the drone immediately disintegrates.

actions.name: Activate Restock Drone
actions.detail: Clear 1d6 heat and one condition, and reloading one Loading weapon. After being activated, the drone immediately disintegrates.

data.description: Reliable and sturdy drones carrying integrated printers, restock drones allow for limited logistical flexibility via autosalvage. The bulk of a restock drone is made of RawMat, a blend of silicates and metallic materials that the drone processes into replacement parts and repair kits. This is why pilots often joke that restock drones are, simply put, “mech snacks”.

data.name: MULE Harness
data.effect:
Extra mounts, straps, and hard points allow other characters to climb and ride your mech. Adjacent, non-Immobilized characters can climb onto your mech as a quick action. While riding, they occupy the same space as you, move when you move (even if they’re Slowed), and benefit from soft cover. If you or a rider are knocked Prone, Stunned, Immobilized, or destroyed, they land Prone in adjacent spaces. Riders can climb down as part of any movement away, but can only climb onto your mech as a quick action.
You can carry riders of a combined Size equal to your Size, minus Size 1/2 (e.g., if your mech is Size 1 you can carry one Size 1/2 character; if it is Size 2, you can carry a Size 1 character and a Size 1/2 character).
data.description: The Multiple User, Light Entanglement (MULE) Harness is a mass-produced version of a common battlefield modification that allows friendly soldiers to ride along on a chassis. Some systems are large enough to allow smaller chassis to accompany larger chassis; typically, these variants are employed in high altitude, low orbit insertions where reduced radar presence is required.

data.name: Custom Paint Job
data.effect:
When you take structure damage, roll 1d6. On a 6, you return to 1 HP and ignore the damage – the hit simply ‘scratched your paint’.
This system can only be used once before each Full Repair, and is not a valid target for system destruction.

active_effects.name: Custom Paint Job
active_effects.detail: When you take structure damage, roll 1d6. On a 6, you return to 1 HP and ignore the damage – the hit simply ‘scratched your paint’. This system can only be used once before each Full Repair.

data.name: Personalizations
data.effect:
You gain +2 HP and, in consultation with the GM, you may establish a minor modification you have made to your mech.
This mod has no numerical benefit beyond the additional HP it grants, but could provide other useful effects. If the GM agrees that this mod would help with either a pilot or mech skill check, you gain +1 Accuracy for that check.

active_effects.name: Personalizations
active_effects.detail: Your customizations relevant to a pilot or mech skill check, gains +1 Accuracy (GM discretion).

actions.name: Frag Grenade
actions.detail: Throw a Frag Grenade within Range 5. All characters within a Blast 1 area must pass an Agility save or take 1d6 Explosive damage. On a success, they take half damage.

deployables.name: Explosive Mine
deployables.detail: All characters within a Burst 1 area must pass an Agility save or take 2d6 Explosive damage. On a success, they take half damage.

data.name: Rocket-Propelled Grenade
data.description:
Much like GMS mechs, GMS weapons are reliable galactic standards, made using interchangeable parts and built to withstand almost any conditions. There are three lines currently in production.
The Type-III (T-3) line is made up of heavy weapons, ordnance, and other exotic, specialized, or massive weapons. A broad classification, the T-3 range includes conventional-kinetic anti-materiel rifles, super-rapid cycling pulse rifles, missile racks, cannons, and drone nexuses – “hive”style launchers that serve as miniature factory, hangar, and deployment systems for portable drones. The classification also includes the fearsome “segment knife”, a system that uses flash-printing to produce disposable edged weapons in a vicinity around the user.

data.name: Missile Rack
data.description:
Much like GMS mechs, GMS weapons are reliable galactic standards, made using interchangeable parts and built to withstand almost any conditions. There are three lines currently in production.
The Type-III (T-3) line is made up of heavy weapons, ordnance, and other exotic, specialized, or massive weapons. The classification also includes the fearsome “segment knife”, a system that uses flash-printing to produce disposable edged weapons in a vicinity around the user.

data.name: Latch Drone
data.effect: This weapon can’t make normal attacks. Instead, choose an allied mech within Range and line of sight and make a ranged attack against Evasion 8. On a hit, either you or your target may spend 1 Repair to restore half your target’s HP.

data.name: Blow Something Up
data.description: Use explosives to totally wreck something or turn it into an enormous fireball.
data.detail: Use explosives (improvised or otherwise), weapons, or maybe just good old fashion brawn to totally wreck something or turn it into an enormous fireball (maybe a wall, sensor array, outpost, reactor core - the good stuff). Probably not to be used against people unless they’re incidentally in the way.

data.name: Hack or Fix
data.description: Repair a device or faulty system; alternatively, hack it wide open, or totally wreck, disable or sabotage it.
data.detail: Repair a device or faulty system. Alternately, hack it wide open, or totally wreck, disable or sabotage it. You can use this for hacking or safeguarding electronic systems, such as electronic door locks, computer systems, omninet webs, or NHP coffins.

data.name: Invent or Create
data.description: Invent new devices, tools, or approaches to problems.
data.detail: Generally speaking, you need tools and supplies to invent or create something successfully. Use this with many downtime actions to work on projects. You can also use it in the spur of the moment to invent new devices, tools, or approaches to something (improvised explosives, gear, disguises, or some similar).

data.name: Patch
data.description: Apply medical knowledge to medicate or diagnose.
data.detail: Apply your medical knowledge to administer medication, bandage a wound, staunch bleeding, suture, cauterize, neutralize poison, or resuscitate. Alternately, you could use it to diagnose or study disease, pathogens, or illness.

data.name: Stay Cool
data.description: Perform a task that requires concentration, dexterity, speed, or precision under pressure.
data.detail: Do something that requires concentration, speed, or intense precision under pressure, like picking a lock as your squad trades fire with encroaching guards, avoiding a hostile memetic code while hacking a secure console, carefully disarming an explosive, or unjamming a gun under fire. If you’ve got to do something complicated in a high stress situation without messing up (and possibly not even breaking a sweat) this is the action to use.

data.name: Demolitionist
data.terse: Improve your grenades and mines to fly further and hit harder
data.description: Explosives and warfare go together like alcohol and bad decisions. The power of a bomb in the palm of your hand is a great equalizer, and a well-placed satchel charge or two has brought even the mightiest of fortifications tumbling down. Forget bullets with names etched on them, the packages you deliver go out addressed “To Whom It May Concern,” and you’ve got plenty to go around.

ranks.name: Frag and Clear
ranks.description: When you use a Grenade, you may choose one character in the affected area to ignore its effects. Additionally, at the end of each scene, you restore 1 charge to each Limited system with the Mine tag for each undetonated Mine you deployed from that system.

active_effects.name: Frag and Clear
active_effects.detail: When you use a Grenade, you may choose one character in the affected area to ignore its effects. At the end of each scene, you restore 1 charge to each Limited system with the Mine tag for each undetonated Mine you deployed from that system.

synergies.detail: When you use a Grenade, you may choose one character in the affected area to ignore its effects.
At the end of each scene, you restore 1 charge to each Limited system with the Mine tag for each undetonated Mine you deployed from that system.

ranks.name: Quarterback
ranks.description: Your Grenades gain +3 Range, and you can plant Mines up to Range 3 (or add +3 Range to them if they have one). Additionally, you do not require line of sight for Grenades and Mines as long as it's possible to trace a path to the target.

active_effects.name: Quarterback
active_effects.detail: Your Grenades gain +3 Range, and you can plant Mines up to Range 3 (or add +3 Range). You do not require line of sight for Grenades and Mines as long as it's possible to trace a path to the target.

synergies.detail: Your Grenades gain +3 Range, you can plant Mines up to Range 3 (or add +3 Range), and you do not require line of sight for Grenades and Mines as long as it's possible to trace a path to the target.

ranks.name: Fire in the Hole
ranks.description:
Your explosive charges have been enhanced with customized payloads. 1/round, you may choose one of the following:

  • When you throw a Grenade, up to three characters within Range 3 of the targeted space take 2 explosive damage and are knocked back 1 space in a direction of your choice by explosive shrapnel.
  • When a character fails a save against one of your Mines, they take +1d6 explosive bonus damage. If the mine deals no damage normally when detonated, whether it forces a save or not, one character in the affected area takes 1d6 explosive damage instead.

active_effects.name: Fire in the Hole
active_effects.detail: 1/round, choose one: When you throw a Grenade, up to three characters within Range 3 of the targeted space take 2 explosive damage and are knocked back 1 space; OR when a character fails a save against your Mine, they take +1d6 explosive bonus damage (or 1d6 if the mine normally deals no damage).

synergies.detail: 1/round, when you throw a Grenade, up to three characters within Range 3 of the targeted space take 2 explosive damage and are knocked back 1 space in a direction of your choice.

1/round, when a character fails a save against one of your Mines, they take +1d6 explosive bonus damage. If the mine deals no damage normally, one character in the affected area takes 1d6 explosive damage instead.

data.name: House Guard
data.terse: Improve your ability to defend your allies.
data.description: You fight at the side of your allies, your mech a bulwark that grants them unbreakable resolve and bolsters them up to greater glory.

ranks.name: Front Rank
ranks.description: You count as adjacent when you are within Range 2 for the purposes of your effects on allied characters (from your traits, talents, systems, or weapons) that require adjacency to your mech.

active_effects.name: Front Rank
active_effects.detail: You count as adjacent when you are within Range 2 for the purposes of your effects on allied characters (from your traits, talents, systems, or weapons) that require adjacency to your mech.

ranks.name: Greater Guardian
ranks.description: Your mech gains the Guardian trait if it doesn’t already have it (adjacent allies can use your mech as hard cover). Guardian now additionally grants soft cover to all adjacent allies from all directions.

active_effects.name: Greater Guardian
active_effects.detail: Your mech gains the Guardian trait if it doesn’t already have it (adjacent allies can use your mech as hard cover). Guardian now additionally grants soft cover to all adjacent allies from all directions.

ranks.name: Shield of the Legion
ranks.description: 1/round, when you reduce damage to an allied character, cancel an attack against them, or cause one to miss, you may deal 2 energy damage to the attacker and knock them Prone.

actions.name: Shield of the Legion
actions.detail: When you reduce damage to an allied character, cancel an attack against them, or cause one to miss, you may deal 2 energy damage to the attacker and knock them Prone.

data.name: Grease Monkey
data.terse: Get more out of Limited systems, repairs, and the Stabilize action
data.description: Eel knows more about the inner workings of a mech than most mechanics. To them, the beast they pilot is more than a machine: it’s a living thing, in need of tender care given by a wise and steady hand. Eel maintains their own house and keeps their own mech in line, both on the battlefield and off. The mechanics back at base come to them with questions, but usually prefer to stay away – there’s something spooky about how Eel's beast runs.

ranks.name: Unsanctioned Capacity Upgrade
ranks.description: While resting, you can spend 2 Repairs to replenish 1 use of all Limited weapons and systems.

ranks.name: Machine Bond
ranks.description: When you STABILIZE, you clear all IMPAIRED, JAMMED, IMMOBILIZED, SLOWED, and LOCK ON conditions that weren’t caused by your own systems, talents, etc.

active_effects.name: Machine Bond
active_effects.detail: When you STABILIZE, you clear all IMPAIRED, JAMMED, IMMOBILIZED, SLOWED, and LOCK ON conditions that weren’t caused by your own systems, talents, etc.

synergies.detail: When you STABILIZE, you clear all IMPAIRED, JAMMED, IMMOBILIZED, SLOWED, and LOCK ON conditions that weren’t caused by your own systems, talents, etc.

ranks.name: Friends in High Places
ranks.description: Once per mission while resting, you can call in a supply drop. You and your allies may replenish 1 use of all Limited weapons and systems and restore 1 Structure. This doesn’t require any Repairs and can be used even if you have reached your Repair Cap.

synergies.detail: Once per mission while resting, you can call in a supply drop. You and your allies may replenish 1 use of all Limited weapons and systems and restore 1 Structure. This doesn’t require any Repairs and can be used even if you have reached your Repair Cap.

data.name: Drone Commander
data.terse: Improve and empower your Drone Systems to help allies and hurt enemies
data.description: For a pilot fresh out of boot, keeping a drone swarm in line is like trying to carry water with a net. If they seem to have a mind of their own, it’s because they do, and it’s not that smart. Clymene Kanalakos’s initial frustration was enough to get her practicing, and practice pays off. Now, her swarm obeys almost before she orders – an unnerving development, but a useful one. The swarm is hers.

ranks.name: Shepherd
ranks.description: Your Drone systems gain +5 HP. Additionally, gain the Shepherd Drone Protocol.

synergies.detail: This Drone system gains +5 HP. As a protocol, you may move one this drone up to 4 spaces if it is within Sensors.

actions.name: Shepherd Drone
actions.detail: Move a drone you control up to 4 spaces if it is within Sensors.

ranks.name: Energized Swarm
ranks.description: 1/round, when you make an attack that consumes the Lock On condition, your Drones immediately emit a vicious pulse of energy. All characters of your choice within Burst 1 areas centered on each of your drones take 1d6 Energy damage. Each character can only be affected by the pulse from one drone, even if the areas overlap.

active_effects.name: Energized Swarm
active_effects.detail: 1/round, when you make an attack that consumes the Lock On condition, your Drones immediately emit a vicious pulse of energy. All characters of your choice within Burst 1 areas centered on each of your drones take 1d6 Energy damage. Each character can only be affected by the pulse from one drone, even if the areas overlap.
active_effects.condition: You make an attack that consumes the Lock On condition

actions.name: Invigorate
actions.detail: Send a pulse of energy to an allied character (including Drones) within Range 3, drawing a Line to them. You may extend the pulse from your target to another allied character, extending the Line to them, as long as they are within Range 3, and you may continue extending the pulse (and Line) like this as long as you don’t target the same character twice. Allied characters who are used as pulse targets or are in the Line’s path gain 4 Overshield; hostile characters in the Line’s path take 2 Energy damage instead.

reserves.name: Skill Point
reserves.label: Bonus
reserves.description: Add a Skill Point to gain or improve a skill, typically as part of the "Get Focused" Downtime Action.

data.name: The Pathfinder
major_ideals: I addressed challenges with curiosity, exploration, or understanding.
I expressed my heritage, background, or beliefs through my actions.
I struggled with issues from my burdens or background.
minor_ideals: I smelled, heard, or tasted something new.
I learned a new skill or trade, or gained a new level of mastery in one I already knew.
I met and conversed with an expert.
I beheld a unique, interesting, or beautiful sight.

questions.question: What gives you your power?
options: A star map given to you long ago by an old friend.
Years spent out in the wilderness, mapping the mountains.
Many years on a freighter, and many worlds passed by.

questions.question: Where have you traveled in your dreams?
options: Deep into the molten core of a supernova.
A still, black pool in the deep forest.

powers.name: Momentum
powers.description:
When you survey a situation, ask one of the following questions and get a truthful answer from the GM:
  • How do I think I can get around this obstacle?
  • What’s the most direct way forward?
  • Which way do I feel I should be moving?
You or an ally of your choice gets +1 Accuracy on their next skill check acting on the answer.

powers.name: Saddleborn
powers.description: Gain +1 Accuracy and increased effect to all skill checks related to the use, driving, piloting, and upkeep of vehicles or mounts of any kind. This includes animals like horses.

powers.name: Dabbler
powers.description: Gain +2 to a trigger of your choice, up to a max of +6. You can change this bonus around at the end of each downtime.

powers.name: Feet Up
powers.description: You can forgo any downtime action, including your free Heal Burdens action, to clear 3 Stress.

powers.name: Freesoul
powers.description: You can escape from any restraint, shackle, hold, or prison cell without rolling. Nobody can hold, grab, or restrain you unless you let them. You can choose to conceal this ability if you wish.

powers.name: Beginner’s Luck
powers.description: When you try an activity or skill you’ve never tried before, you get +1 Accuracy and increased effect to checks related to that skill for the rest of the session. This only ever works once for each activity or skill.

powers.name: Lightspeed
powers.description:
When you need to go really, really fast, name your method, your destination, and tell the GM you’re pulling out all the stops. You and any of your allies nearby can get there faster than anyone else has before, and can easily outrun anyone you’re running from or trying to pursue. Don’t roll – you do it – but the GM chooses two:
  • You and your allies are exhausted and take 1 Stress.
  • You go off course and end up close to your destination, but not quite there.
  • Your vehicle, mount, or method of travel is completely busted and will need repair.

powers.name: Lay Burdens
powers.description: Fill in a segment of all burdens when using Heal Burdens for free. If you are healing in a different location than your last downtime, tick another segment on any one burden.

powers.name: Renaissance
powers.description: At the start of any session, pick one of your triggers. You become an expert at that skill. When you roll it, roll two d20s and pick the highest for the final result. You must pick a new trigger each session, and can’t pick the same one twice in a row

powers.name: Feel the Air
powers.description:
You can ask the GM up to three of the following about any location you arrive at and receive truthful answers:
  • Who lives here or has passed through recently, and where can I find them?
  • Who owns this place, or wants to, and where can I talk to them?
  • What part of this place do people avoid, and why?
Gain +1 Accuracy and increased effect on your next check acting on the answers.If you ask only one question, heal 1 Stress.

powers.name: Boon of the Traveler
powers.prerequisite: If you have two or more powers from this bond, you can choose a power from any other bond instead of one from this bond when you would gain a power. You can do this twice. If you have at least one veteran power, gain the Boon of the Traveler.
powers.description: At the end of each session, if you were inspired by the sights, smells, sounds, or sensations of a particular place, describe them. Give someone you shared them with 1 XP.

powers.name: Long Road Home
powers.prerequisite: You may only gain this power If you’ve taken four powers from this bond, including the Veteran Power.
powers.description:
Name a location you’ve been in the last three days. You can make your way back there without rolling. The GM will determine the following about the journey there:
  • Was it a long or arduous journey?
  • Was the location dangerous, defended, or contested?
  • Were you being pursued, tracked, or hunted?
For every “yes” answer, take 2 Stress; however, at the beginning of the next scene, you and up to ten other willing people arrive safely there.Don’t worry about playing out the journey(just ‘cut’ to the next scene as you are arriving) and work backwards to figure out how you got there.

bondPowers.name: Beginner’s Luck
bondPowers.description: When you try an activity or skill you’ve never tried before, you get +1 Accuracy and increased effect to checks related to that skill for the rest of the session. This only ever works once for each activity or skill.
